$comment: REGISTERED MUTATIONS — the evidence behind every @regression test in tests/**.
WHY: two regression tests written during the 11.33.1 session passed with the bug fully
restored. They were vacuous, and only a hand-run mutation caught that. A regression test that
was never seen failing is a claim, not a check — so the claim is written down here in a form a
machine can re-run: `pnpm run check:mutations` applies each mutation, runs the specs that claim
to catch it, and REQUIRES them to go red.
Not part of `pnpm run check` (it deliberately breaks the source and re-runs suites; it belongs
in review and on the publish path, not in every inner loop). It is kept honest without running,
though: tests/unit/regression-evidence.spec.ts asserts that every `find` still matches its
target EXACTLY ONCE, so a mutation that has rotted into a silent no-op fails the normal suite.
id       referenced from the @seen-failing line of the tests it belongs to
file     path relative to the repository root
after    optional anchor; the search starts here (disambiguates identical lines in one file)
find     literal text, must occur exactly once in the search window
replace  what it becomes — the defect, reconstructed
specs    the spec files that MUST fail once the mutation is applied
driverSpecific  true when only some storage drivers are affected; `drivers` names them

mutations.defect: 11.33.1 — deleteFileByName() authorized the caller and then re-resolved the file with an EMPTY context, so an overridden checkRights() was asked two different questions about one request and the owner was told `File not found`.
11.33.0 — getRawFileInfoByName() consulted S3 and GridFS but not the filesystem store, so a by-name ownership rule authorized against a different file set than the download route served.
11.33.0 — the S3 metadata lookups were gated on the ACTIVE driver instead of on whether S3 is usable, so adopting S3 kept GridFS readable while switching back turned every S3-stored file into a 404.

11.33.1 — duplicateByName() accepted no serviceOptions at all and re-resolved the source with an EMPTY context, so under a fail-closed checkRights() the owner's own duplicate was refused (and on the GridFS driver the method bypassed checkRights() entirely and copied unchecked).

11.33.1 — duplicateById() re-resolved the source with an EMPTY context and then dereferenced the null it got back (`file.filename`), so a fail-closed checkRights() produced a TypeError where a 404 belongs — under every storage driver.

mutations.defect: 11.33.1 — deleteFile() fell through to the GridFS driver for an unknown id and surfaced its MongoRuntimeError ('File not found for id …') as an HTTP 500, while its by-name sibling answered a clean 404 for the same condition.

11.33.1 — sortMergedFileInfo() read a sort key with `doc[field]`, so a DOTTED path (metadata.ownerId) was undefined for every row: each store sorted correctly and the merge then tied everything, leaving the page grouped by store. Paging over that returns the WRONG ROWS, not merely the wrong order.
mutations.find:
const left = this.readSortField(a, field);
        const right = this.readSortField(b, field);
mutations.replace:
const left = a?.[field];
        const right = b?.[field];

mutations.defect: 11.33.1 — GridFS keeps contentType inside `metadata` while s3-files / filesystem-files carry it at the document root, so findFileInfo() filtered on contentType matched every S3/filesystem file and NO GridFS file: nothing at all on the default driver, and every pre-switch file silently dropped on any other.

11.33.1 — writeFileFromStream() listened for errors on the DESTINATION stream only. pipe() does not forward source errors, so an aborted upload emitted an unhandled 'error' — an uncaught exception that ends the PROCESS. The same abort was a rejected promise under the S3 and filesystem drivers.

11.33.x — a COMPLETED tus upload's staged object is not an incomplete multipart, so no bucket lifecycle rule reclaims it. Without the explicit cleanup every finished upload leaves a full second copy of itself behind, in a bucket that by default IS the file bucket.

11.33.1 — CoreS3Service.putObject() handed a known-length body stream straight to the AWS SDK, which pipes it into its HTTP request without listening on the SOURCE. A failing body was therefore an unhandled 'error' event — an uncaught exception that ends the process. Reachable from tus finalization into S3, the one upload path that does not buffer first.

11.33.x — the Hub's Files panel read `fs.files` alone, so under `file.storage: 's3'` or 'filesystem' it reported 0 files and could not delete anything. In an operator cockpit a confident wrong answer is worse than an honest gap: it is the tool somebody opens BECAUSE they are unsure whether an upload landed.

mutations.defect: 11.34.0 — an S3-backed delete must REFUSE when CoreS3Service is unavailable. Deleting the metadata document while the object stays in the bucket produces an orphan nothing can find again — unrecoverable in a way that 'try again with S3 configured' is not.

11.34.0 — the Files panel merges three stores, so the union must be re-sorted before the page is cut. Without it the listing comes back GROUPED BY STORE, and `skip`/`limit` over that returns the wrong ROWS — the same defect sortMergedFileInfo() was fixed for, one layer up.

11.34.1 — MapAndValidatePipe built every message from constraintInstance.defaultMessage() alone, so a custom `message` in ValidationOptions (IsIn([...], { message: '...' })) was silently dropped and the client saw the generic default instead.
mutations.find:
let messageTemplate: string | ((args: ValidationArguments) => string) | undefined =
                        metadata.message as string | ((args: ValidationArguments) => string) | undefined;
mutations.replace: let messageTemplate: string | ((args: ValidationArguments) => string) | undefined;

mutations.defect: 11.34.1 — only $property was substituted, so built-in default messages reached API clients with raw placeholders: "each value in roles must be one of the following values: $constraint1".

11.34.1 — the same custom-message gap existed on the non-customValidation path, which since class-validator 0.13 is reached by @IsDefined alone: its hardcoded message won over the message the developer wrote.

mutations.defect: 11.34.1 — the message renderer is a port of class-validator internals, and a port drifts silently: vendor-mode consumers resolve their OWN class-validator, so src/core/ can meet a version this repo never installed. Dropping $target is the smallest such drift, and no e2e case reaches that token — only the mirror invariant test does.
